Organize a meeting in person with your boss and make sure you have colleagues in your corner if you want to obtain a salary increase, a career expert revealed.
And you should never make a salary increase of a simple application for itself or not, according to Nicola Weatherhead, vice president, people’s operations and talent acquisition in the Stepstone group.
In December, salary growth increased for the first time in more than a year, figures from the National Statistics Office were shown.
The payment of the private sector grew at an annual rate of 5.4%, while in the public sector it was 4.3%.
But if you still yearn for a salary increase, be sure to do your homework, said Weatherhead.
Employers will be surprised with the increase in national insurance this year, which will cost around £ 800 for each minimum wage employee and more for workers who earn greater salaries.

The increase in national insurance enters into force in April, which means that it has months to consider options before requesting an increase.

Rather, ask if you can create a path that will take you to your desired salary.
I should say ‘I am committed to creating a significant value for the company, and I would like to discuss how we can establish a road map that ensures that a fair part of that value is returned. I understand that this may not happen overnight, but I am anxious to understand the steps we can take to achieve this together, “according to Mrs. Weatherhead
Position your question in this way will emphasize mutual benefits and show your dedication to the company, while opening the door for a salary increase.

“You are working in a business at the end of the day,” said the career expert.
‘Stay away from comparing yourself to your colleagues or discussing the wages of others. In addition, refrain from making demands or ultimatums, since this can force your relationship with your employer. Instead, grant in your achievements, value and growth potential, and maintain a respectful and professional tone throughout the conversation.
Ask your manager for specific reasons if they reject your salary increase application.
If you know how to improve, you can establish realistic objectives and discuss a timeline for an increase in the future. This will show that it is committed.
Have an honest conversation with your boss if you feel you are not progressing. Here it would be a good time to refer to the salaries you have seen elsewhere.
